switchable.label: New buy ideas
switchable.explain: A message when the bot or the brain finds a stock worth buying, or a brain idea is waiting for your OK. Turning it off only stops the phone message: the ideas still appear in the app and nothing about what is bought changes.

switchable.label: Practice buys
switchable.explain: A message when the bot buys a stock with pretend (paper) money. Buys with real money always message you.

switchable.label: Score slipping on a stock you hold
switchable.explain: An early heads-up when the model's score for a stock you hold gets weaker. It is a warning, not a sell: the stop-loss keeps protecting the stock, and every sell message always reaches you.

switchable.label: End-of-day summary
switchable.explain: One message after the market closes with the day's profit or loss and what is held.

switchable.label: Weekly brain report
switchable.explain: Saturday's checklist on how the brain did this week. The same report is on the System page.

switchable.label: App restarted / Zerodha login worked
switchable.explain: A message when the app starts or stops (for example after an update) and when a Zerodha login succeeded. Login problems always message you.

always_on.label: Sells and stop-losses
always_on.explain: When a stock you hold hits its stop-loss, target or time limit, is sold, or should be sold. You may need to act quickly, so this can't be switched off or delayed.

always_on.label: Real-money orders
always_on.explain: Every real buy or sell sent to your Zerodha account, any order Zerodha refused or cancelled, and an approved idea that could not be bought. Real money is involved.

always_on.label: Safety stops on buying
always_on.explain: When a safety rule stops new buys, for example the account fell 15% from its best value. You need to know the bot has stopped buying.

always_on.label: Zerodha login problems
always_on.explain: When the bot is not logged in to Zerodha. Without it prices stop updating and stop-losses are not checked.

always_on.label: Something broke
always_on.explain: A job failed, market data is missing, the server disk is filling up, or errors are piling up. These need fixing before they cost money.
